cards.title: Borrowed Authority
cards.instruction: Project confident authority while quietly working to keep everyone cooperative. Your confidence depends on their cooperation.

cards.title: Acknowledge the Disrespect
cards.instruction: Make someone apologize for the disrespect to your position, not merely for what happened.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I'd like to keep this voluntary. You told the trainees their head trainer was an idiot. I want an apology. Please.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I'm still in charge; we can make an adjustment. For undermining their head trainer. They still need to follow my instructions.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I'll email them after tomorrow's drill.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Read it to them before the drill. My whistle isn't going to outrank 'idiot' on its own.

mechanism: A asserts training leadership while negotiating apology wording and format so trainees hear respect for the role before following the next drill.
confusable: Unlike a general apology for failure, A wants the undermined position repaired; confident command depends on B helping restore it.
comparison: Public trainee instruction and pre-drill message differ from a meeting chair accepting a quiet title-specific apology.
seedUse: Use D51-b failed drill/idiot/trainee message and S02-a allowing an adjusted method to sustain authority.
